title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
description: Investigate and respond to the Kobalos malware incident in your network.

levels.title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
levels.content:
The Kobalos malware has been detected in your network. It is a complex backdoor that targets high-performance computing (HPC) clusters and other high-profile systems. Kobalos grants remote access to the file system, provides the ability to spawn terminal sessions, and allows proxying connections to other Kobalos-infected servers. It also includes a credential stealer component that captures SSH credentials.

Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox environment via the provided cloud interface. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.
levels.local_content: Instructions for local sandbox usage. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate the suspicious service that is communicating with the C2 server.

The Kobalos malware is known to create persistent services for communication. Investigate the services running on the `target` host and identify the suspicious one. The flag is the name of the suspicious service.
levels.solution:
Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

The suspicious service is named `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often creates persistent services to maintain communication with command and control servers.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check the systemd services for any unusual or recently created services.

levels.title: Identify Data Exfiltration Mechanism
levels.content:
Identify the data exfiltration mechanism used by the malware.

Kobalos is known to exfiltrate data from infected systems. Investigate the network connections and file transfers on the `target` host to identify the data exfiltration mechanism. The flag is the filename used for data exfiltration.
levels.solution:
Check the logs for any unusual outbound connections or file transfers.

The data exfiltration mechanism is using the `payload-transfer.sh` script.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Data exfiltration often involves scripts or processes that transfer data to external servers.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check the logs for any unusual outbound connections or file transfers.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The data exfiltration mechanism is using the `payload-transfer.sh` script.

levels.title: Contain C2 Communication
levels.content:
Contain the C2 communication by blocking the suspicious port.

To prevent further communication with the C2 server, you need to block the port used by the malicious service. Identify the port and implement a containment strategy. The flag is the port number used for C2 communication.
levels.solution:
Use firewall rules or service configuration to block the port.

The port number used for C2 communication is `7070`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Blocking communication with the command and control server is crucial to contain the malware.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use firewall rules or service configuration to block the port.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The port number used for C2 communication is `7070`.
